name: InSight
significance: InSight was launched to probe Mars' deep interior -- crust, mantle, and core -- because understanding how a rocky planet differentiates and cools is essential to understanding how Earth and other rocky planets formed, a question surface geology alone cannot answer. It was the first mission to place a seismometer on the surface of another planet and to combine it with a dedicated heat-flow probe for direct measurement of marsquakes and interior temperature. Over its mission it detected more than 1,300 marsquakes, revealed that Mars has a surprisingly large, largely molten outer core with a thin, small solid inner core, and mapped crust and mantle layering, showing Mars' crust is thinner and more fractured than models predicted -- findings that reshaped theories of terrestrial planet formation.
statusNote: Mission ended 2022-12-21 when dust accumulation on solar panels reduced power below operating threshold.
